brief: UBS sales note: the circuit breakers it had flagged as catalysts to fresh highs (rate pressures spiraling into funding pressures, oil rising on the Mideast conflict, weak hyperscaler earnings, Democrats winning the midterms) have not materialized over the past two months. Instead AI repriced violently lower as investors demanded a bigger discount for AI risk, and flows rotated out of Tech, out of equities broadly, into credit, where AI exposure is growing fast. That rotation peaked Thursday with a record 365bn of systematic SPX sell flow (NDX -203bn), with no sponsorship for a Friday reversal. Most of that selling is now behind the market, but the bigger issue is the absence of long-only demand, which UBS calls the focal point for flows from here. Hyperscalers have outperformed the broader AI complex and neoclouds, but UBS sees that as overextended and expects semis to catch up: semis beat a flat hyperscaler basket by 5% Friday. Healthcare and staples are now vulnerable as the quality rotation fades. VIX's cross-asset score hit 96% Thursday, a capitulatory reading. Next catalysts are CPI and NVDA earnings on the 17th, both pricing roughly 1% SPX moves, with a 10Y retest after strong NFP a headwind.
